summary: The Emeya is Lotus's electric four-door hyper-GT, and Australian reviewers agree it is a genuinely resolved luxury EV — CarExpert praises air suspension that "breathes nicely with the road" rather than feeling floaty, and CarsGuide rates the chassis agile enough to hold its own against a Porsche Taycan while offering far more rear legroom. Where they part company is on whether it is still a Lotus: at 2480-2575kg CarsGuide argues it "abandons Lotus' lightweight principles" and that the heaviness dulls its edge. The bigger buyer risk is commercial rather than dynamic — Australia bought 5 in 2024, 3 in 2025 and 2 to October 2026; the range-topping 900 (formerly R, $259,990) is not listed here because it sits above the app's price ceiling.
pros: Wheelbase is roughly 200mm longer than a Porsche Taycan's, so rear legroom is genuinely adult-sized where the Taycan and Audi e-tron GT are cramped
800V architecture charges at up to 350kW for a 10-80 per cent top-up in about 14 minutes, comfortably quicker than a Taycan on the same charger
Liftback tailgate gives 509 litres behind the rear seats (1388 litres folded, measured to the roof), plus a 34-litre frunk — far more usable than the sedan-booted e-tron GT
Unconditional five-year/150,000km vehicle warranty with eight years/200,000km on the battery, no dealer-servicing strings attached
Entry 600 on 20-inch wheels is rated at 610km WLTP from a 98.9kWh usable pack (580km for the 21-inch 600 SE), well ahead of the 506km BMW i5 M60 at a similar price
cons: Australian volume is effectively nil — 5 sales in 2024, 3 in 2025 and 2 to October 2026 — so there is almost no used-buyer base and resale risk is severe
Only five Lotus retailers nationally (Brisbane, Sydney, Melbourne, Adelaide, Perth), meaning no franchised service or warranty support outside a capital city
Documented heavy discounting overseas: Carscoops reported in May 2026 that a London Lotus dealer had cut a new Emeya R from £140,105 to £89,950, about 40 per cent off
Kerb weight of 2480-2575kg is close to a large SUV, and CarsGuide judges that the mass blunts the agility the badge implies

Lotus Australia publishes no prices on its website or configurator; the $189,990 and $209,990 figures are the 2024 launch prices still quoted by CarExpert, so confirm the current list price with a retailer
